subject: Dedicated pool queueing grace period request — Helios AI

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@helios-ai.com>

Cc: ops@helios-ai.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool: observed queueing spikes + ask for grace window

Hi Jordan —

Quick summary: over the last two nights we observed a sustained increase in queueing on our dedicated pool (pool-id: hls-prod-2). Tail latency jumped to ~3.2s for short responses between 01:00–03:30 UTC and a subset of real-time inference requests hit throttles intermittently. We shipped a feature yesterday that briefly increased concurrent short calls; it looks like the overlap with nightly batch jobs is causing transient contention on reserved GPUs.

We need two things from Redwood: a temporary carveout/grace period while we throttle rollout on our side (48–72 hours), and a short-term mitigation (either temporary headroom or an SLA-friendly fallback so our realtime customers don’t see 5xx or heavy latency spikes). We may ask for a one-time credit depending on measurable user impact.

I attached a small sample log (helios_queue_sample_Mar31.log) showing queued/request spikes with timestamps and request IDs.

Can you advise next steps and whether Redwood can enable any short-term queue-priority rule or headroom to prevent preemption/throttling during this launch window?

Thanks —
Sam Ortiz
Director, Platform Ops
Helios AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: observed queueing spikes + ask for grace window

Thanks — dug into the logs Sam attached and correlated with internal traces. Short version: the reserved GPU pool (hls-prod-2) enforces per-tenant concurrency plus a background nightly batch that currently uses nonzero reserved capacity. When your short-request concurrency spiked it pushed the pool into queuing behavior that favored long-running batch kernels, yielding the tail latency increase you saw.

Immediate options (fastest to deploy):
- Temporary "burst tokens" for Helios (pre-provisioned token budget that allows short bursts up to 150% of baseline reserved concurrency for 48 hours). Tokens are tracked and decay; no code change required on your side.
- Short-term priority rule: elevate realtime traffic (routes matching /v1/infer/short) above batch during the carveout window. This requires a config flip and a 5–10 minute rollout.
- Preemption disable for batch jobs inside the pool for up to 24 hours (not recommended beyond that due to fairness).

Recommended approach: enable burst tokens + priority rule for 48 hours. This gives you headroom and minimal risk to other tenants. We can also add a temporary fallback route to a compatible burst model (quantized variant) if queueing persists.

SLA implications / measurable commitments for the 48h window: we can guarantee that realtime p95 latency for your short-route will stay under 800ms for the carved period provided burst usage stays < 60% of allocated tokens. If usage exceeds that, we will notify and fallback to a secondary model to preserve availability. That p95 guarantee is operational (we'll monitor and produce a SOC-like report for the window).

I attached the proposed addendum language (proposed_addendum_helios_dedicated.docx) with exact thresholds, token accounting, and notification cadence. If Helios agrees, we can flip configs tonight and monitor.
